question: What is the primary goal of the surgical scrub process?

options.A: Eliminate all bacteria permanently from deep skin layers
options.B: Soften the skin to prevent tearing of sterile gloves
options.C: Cool down the hands before putting on sterile gloves
options.D: Reduce resident flora and remove transient microorganisms

explanation: The surgical scrub aims to lower bacterial load on the skin surface by targeting transient microbes and reducing resident flora. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why does surgical scrubbing differ from regular everyday handwashing?

options.A: It uses regular bath soap instead of medicated solutions
options.B: It completely sterilizes the living tissue of the hands
options.C: It requires a specific duration and rigorous technique
options.D: It is only performed after the surgical procedure ends

explanation: Surgical scrubbing involves timed steps and specialized friction to lower microbial counts far beyond standard hand hygiene. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why must all rings and watches be removed prior to scrubbing?

options.A: They can easily scratch the patient during surgery
options.B: Hospital policies forbid any metal inside the theatre
options.C: They react chemically with the antiseptic scrub agents
options.D: They trap microorganisms and increase glove puncture risks

explanation: Jewelry creates protected spaces for bacteria accumulation and poses a physical hazard to glove integrity. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: A nurse preparing to scrub notices chipped nail polish. What action is required?

options.A: Remove the polish completely before starting the scrub
options.B: Proceed with the scrub since only artificial nails are banned
options.C: Cover the polish with a fresh layer of clear lacquer
options.D: Wear an extra pair of inner gloves to contain the nails

explanation: Chipped nail polish harbors high concentrations of bacteria and must be completely removed prior to any surgical scrub. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which antiseptic agent is known for providing a long-lasting residual antimicrobial effect on the skin?
explanation: Chlorhexidine binds to the stratum corneum, offering prolonged residual activity against skin microbes. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is a known limitation of povidone-iodine when used for surgical scrubbing?

options.A: Its activity can be reduced by blood and organic matter
options.B: It turns the skin permanently blue upon contact
options.C: It has zero effectiveness against gram-positive bacteria
options.D: It causes immediate chemical burns on intact skin

explanation: Organic debris like blood binds to iodine, neutralizing its antimicrobial effectiveness during surgical procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: In what direction must water and soap run during a surgical scrub?

options.A: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.B: From the elbows down toward the fingertips
options.C: In any direction as long as friction is applied
options.D: From the upper arms inward toward the chest

explanation: Keeping hands elevated ensures dirty water flows away from the surgically clean hands toward the elbows. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why must hands remain elevated higher than the elbows after scrubbing?

options.A: To improve blood circulation to the fingers during surgery
options.B: To allow the antiseptic soap to dry faster in the air
options.C: To prevent unwashed water from running down onto clean hands
options.D: To comply with traditional theatre etiquette and posture rules

explanation: Gravity dictates fluid movement; keeping hands high stops contaminated runoff from the upper arms from contaminating the fingers. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: How should a scrubbed nurse dry their hands and arms before putting on a sterile gown?

options.A: By rubbing vigorously with a standard hospital towel
options.B: By waving the arms rapidly in front of an air dryer
options.C: Allowing them to air dry naturally without any contact
options.D: Using a sterile towel with an aseptic blotting technique

explanation: A sterile towel is used to blot moisture carefully without transferring contaminants from unsterile body parts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: A scrubbed nurse accidentally brushes their forearm against an unsterile door frame. What is the correct action?

options.A: Wipe the area with an alcohol swab and continue entering
options.B: Ask a circulating nurse to spray the area with disinfectant
options.C: Consider the arm contaminated and perform a complete re-scrub
options.D: Ignore the contact since only the hands need to remain sterile

explanation: Any contact with a non-sterile surface breaks the aseptic barrier, requiring the entire scrub process to be repeated. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable practice during surgical scrubbing?

options.A: Using a sterile towel to dry arms before gowning
options.B: Dropping scrubbed hands below the waist level
options.C: Holding hands above the level of the elbow
options.D: Rinsing water off from fingertips to the elbows

explanation: Dropping hands below the waist places them out of the sterile visual field and is a major contamination error. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)

question: What should happen if a scrubbed nurse touches a non-sterile Mayo stand by mistake?

options.A: Scrub the hands again and put on a fresh gown and gloves
options.B: Proceed cautiously without touching any more instruments
options.C: Wipe the glove surface with povidone-iodine solution
options.D: Change the sterile gloves only and proceed with the case

explanation: Touching unsterile equipment compromises the sterility of the barrier, necessitating a complete reset of the scrub and attire. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)
